turns.t: Doctor, I'm Ian, Frank's brother. He won't ask, so I will. He's got a cough every morning, and he's been a smoker for forty years.
It's just a smoker's cough. ~
Frank, I'd like to hear it from you. Tell me about the morning cough.
I cough when I get up. Bring up some phlegm. Then it's gone by mid-morning.
What colour is the phlegm?
White, mostly. A bit grey at times. ~
How many years has this been going on? ~
Years. I can't say exactly. Ten, maybe. ~
Any breathlessness, or wheeze? ~
Going up the stairs, I get puffed. But I'm fifty-eight. ~
He's been puffed for a good while. ~
Any blood in the phlegm?
No. Never.
How much do you smoke?
Twenty a day. Since I was eighteen.
What are you taking?
A blue inhaler. Salbutamol. Two puffs, when I need it. Not often.
Any other conditions?
High blood pressure.
I'll listen to your chest. ~
Go on.
There's a bit of wheeze when you breathe out, and your breathing out takes longer than normal, otherwise clear.
Is it serious? ~

It can't be diagnosed by listening alone. The picture, forty years of smoking, a morning cough with phlegm, and getting puffed on stairs, makes me think of COPD, but I can't be sure until we've tested.
COPD. Is that the one my father had? ~
It's a chronic lung condition caused mostly by smoking. It's treatable. The best treatment is stopping smoking. ~
I know. I've tried. ~
I'd like to arrange a breathing test, spirometry, and a chest X-ray.
When? ~
This week or next. The surgery will ring you. ~
Okay. ~
And I can help you stop, with a stop-smoking service, and medicines that make it much easier. ~
Maybe. ~
Think about it, no pressure. I'd like to see you once the tests are done, in two weeks.
I'll make sure he comes. ~
If you cough up blood, have chest pain, or get very breathless, come at once.
Right. Thank you. ~
